releases.title: Four new website pages for search

notes.text: Four new website pages, each written for a search ski area managers make: Ski area POS, Online lift ticket sales, Terrain park software and Ski area staff scheduling. Each has its own title, description, questions and answers for Google, and is in the menu, the footer, the sitemap and llms.txt.
Shorter search titles on the ski patrol, lift ticket and ski school pages, so Google shows them whole. The product page links to each new page and mentions the card reader.

releases.title: Card reader, lesson cancelling, pin dropping, your own guest types

notes.text: Take cards on a Stripe smart reader at the ticket window. Pair a reader under Billing, then choose Charge on reader at checkout: the guest taps, inserts or swipes, and the money goes straight into your own Stripe account. Refunds work the same as online card payments. If the sale is closed before it finishes, the reader payment is refunded for you.

Cancel a lesson, or every lesson on a storm day. Package lessons get their credit back, lessons paid online are refunded in full to the card, counter sales are listed for a refund at the desk, and every booked guest gets one email. A lesson added by mistake with nobody booked can be deleted instead.

Dropping feature pins in the terrain park waits for a good GPS fix and shows how close it is, drops the pin by itself once the fix is good, and lets you drag it into place. Walk the park drops one feature after another as you reach each one. Each pin shows how it was placed.

Your own guest types, under Products and prices, Guest types. Add types like College or Local, rename them, set the ages that pick them online, hide them and change their order. Your current Adult, Youth, Child, Senior and Military prices carry straight over.

Day by day, under Mountain status, Snow and weather: each finished day is written down every night with the weather at the mountain, new snow, whether you were open, visits, tickets, lessons and revenue. Fill in the past year with one button. This is the history the visitor forecast will learn from.
On a phone, buttons in a list no longer break their words across two lines.

The try page emails a 6-digit code before it builds a demo, so every demo lead is a real address. Codes last 15 minutes, only the newest works, five wrong tries use it up, and throwaway inboxes are turned away. On in production and staging whenever email is set up; TRY_EMAIL_CHECK=off turns it off.
Demo mountains can be built on staging again: the demo builder's own internal requests were being stopped by the staging password page.

releases.title: Verdynt/OS: a new name and a new look

notes.text: DAY/OS is now Verdynt/OS, with a new logo and a dark slate and gold look. Prefer the light look? Choose Light in the account menu. Printing always stays light.
Adding Verdynt/OS to a phone's home screen works again, with the new icon.

releases.title: Every release is checked on staging first

notes.text: Coming to DAY/OS in Help now lists data import from your old system and the new assistants: the snow report, the morning brief, patrol report checks, asking your data and documents, and suggested guest replies.

Staging: a private test copy with its own database, Stripe in test mode, email to the team only and a shared password. deploy.sh now puts a release on staging; promote.sh puts that exact build live after a typed confirmation.
Help now has Coming to DAY/OS: what we're building now, next and later. Tell us what your mountain needs most and it moves up the list.
Choosing who to put on a shift is quicker for a big crew: everyone's availability, training and clashes are now checked several people at a time.
The patrol schedule's who-can-take-this list and the open shifts page load faster on a big roster.
Code sweep: package updates (no known vulnerabilities), unused code removed, patrol access checks for a whole roster in one query, and a smaller container image.

releases.title: Guest payments go to your own Stripe account

notes.text: Guests' card payments (the online shop, lesson payments, date changes and patrol giving) now go straight into your mountain's own Stripe account, and Stripe pays them out to your bank. Connect it under Billing, Guest card payments. Card payments open as soon as Stripe has what it needs.
Billing shows whether guest card payments are on, which Stripe account they go to, and whether payouts are set up. Only the owner can connect or disconnect the account, after confirming it is them.

Stripe Connect: each mountain's guest payments are direct charges on its own Standard account. The console shows each mountain's connection and can set a DAY/OS fee per mountain (a share and a fixed amount, 0 unless set), kept by Stripe and returned in proportion on refunds; gifts never carry it. Events from a mountain's account only ever count for that mountain. Set up the Connect webhook as DEPLOY.md, Guest card payments, describes.
DAY/OS has a new logo: day/os with a mountain peak for the slash. It is on the sign-in screen, at the top of the menu, and as the app icon when you add DAY/OS to a phone's home screen.
The website uses the new logo in its header and footer, its browser icon and its link preview image. The logo files, for light and dark backgrounds, are in public/brand.

The runmyresort.com website is rebuilt for phones: a sticky header, a full-screen menu, a Try the demo and Book a walkthrough bar at the bottom, long feature lists folded behind "What it does", and rows that swipe sideways. Home is about half as long on a phone.

Six pages written for what ski areas search for: ski patrol, lift tickets and passes, ski school, ski rentals, online waivers, and lift and fleet maintenance. Each has its own title, questions and links, and is in the sitemap, the menu and the footer.

Search engines now see the live plans and prices in Home and Pricing, richer structured data on every page, and /llms.txt, a plain summary for AI assistants. The website's styles and script are kept by browsers for a year and refreshed by each release.
The Patrol only plan on Pricing listed "Everything in Resort, plus" with nothing under it. It now lists its own apps.
SummitOps is now called DAY/OS, the operating system for your day. Nothing else changes: your sign-in, your data and every app work as before. The website moves to runmyresort.com.
The website, emails, the app, the console and the link preview image all use the new name. Set the runmyresort.com addresses on the service as DEPLOY.md, Putting the website live, describes.

A Patrol only plan, for a ski patrol that signs up on its own: Patrol and Documents, $149 a month or $1,500 a year. It is on the website's Pricing page, and the Ski patrol page and Contact form take patrol sign-ups.
Runs and lifts in Patrol settings: a patrol without the Lifts and trails app keeps its own list, which cases, trail checks and sweep routes point at.
Import the patrol roster from a spreadsheet (Team, Import from a spreadsheet). People already on the roster are skipped, and leaders and directors are set by hand.

A free read-only login for the ski area (Account, Logins, role Ski area): the patrol's day in numbers and every approved report, nothing else. It uses two-step sign-in and every report it opens is recorded.
On the Patrol only plan, signing in opens Patrol, and the menu shows only what a patrol uses.

Passkeys: sign in with your fingerprint, face or your device's PIN instead of a password and code. Nobody can phish or guess a passkey. Add one in Account, then press "Sign in with a passkey". A passkey also counts as two-step sign-in.

Before sensitive actions you are asked to confirm it is you, even when signed in: refunds over $200, changing someone's role or password, switching a login off, downloading customer, waiver or patient lists, releasing a patient record, changing billing, and weakening sign-in rules. It lasts 10 minutes, and straight after signing in counts.

Account shows where you are signed in and the devices you have used, so you can sign out anywhere else. A sign-in from a new device is emailed to you; without two-step sign-in, a code is emailed first.

Shared terminals: enroll the ticket window, rental counter or other shared computers in Account. Counter, instructor and lift staff then switch in with their username and a personal PIN, so nobody shares a login. A terminal's sign-in ends after 15 minutes unused.
Season end: set the last day of the season under Logins, and seasonal logins stop working after it (owners and managers are never affected). Change one person's date in Edit to bring them back.

Patrollers will need two-step sign-in (a passkey takes a minute), because Patrol holds patient details. Mountains already on SummitOps have two weeks; you will see a reminder until then. Patrol Admins and Managers need it now.
New passwords must be at least 12 characters and must not contain your username, email name or the mountain's name. A short phrase of a few words is easiest.
Console: operators can add passkeys (then they sign in with the passkey only), and changing a mountain now needs it opened first with a reason, for up to 8 hours, recorded in its history.

Signing out now ends the session on the server, so a copy of the sign-in kept on another device stops working too. A session left unused for an hour ends, and changing your password signs you out everywhere else. Everyone signs in again once after this update.
Ten wrong passwords in a row lock that login for 15 minutes, and a password already exposed in a data breach elsewhere can no longer be chosen.
Owners and managers must set up two-step sign-in. You are taken to set it up the next time you sign in; it takes a minute with an authenticator app.
Reports and notes saved on a phone while offline are now locked with a key tied to your login, kept separately for each person, and cannot be read once you sign out.
Uploaded files are checked to be what their name says. Zip files and Office files with macros are no longer accepted.

Close mountain in the console: the mountain is paused and everyone signed out at once, and everything in it is deleted after the export window (60 days unless you choose). Resuming it before then cancels the deletion.

The platform key turns itself off once an operator has two-step sign-in. Console actions and sign-ins are also written to Cloud Logging. The daily job now clears website requests older than two years and old sign-in records.

A one-time security setup script for Google Cloud (bash scripts/harden.sh) and an optional web firewall (bash scripts/cloud-armor.sh). Deploys now stop if a package has a known serious security problem.

Today now opens with the morning board: every lift with why it is open, on hold or cannot open; patrollers on duty and runs checked, with any run on hold and why; tonight's grooming; machines and lifts due for service; and unfilled shifts, open work orders and open incidents. Press any heading or number to open that page. If you chose your own tiles before, add it with Customize.

releases.title: Website search engine setup and a ski patrol page

notes.text: The website is set up for search engines: titles and descriptions for what ski areas search for, one address per page, link previews, a sitemap, and structured data with your live prices and each page's questions. The app and console stay out of search results.
A Ski patrol page on the website, for patrol directors, linked from the menu. Set GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION to prove the website to Google Search Console.

The product website is now part of SummitOps: Home, Product, Pricing, Security, Contact, Privacy and Terms, updated with patrol operations, billing, RFID and the Inbox. It is at /site everywhere, and at the top of its own domain once SITE_HOSTS is set.
Pricing on the website comes from the console's Plans and prices, so changing a price there changes the website. The launch plans and add-ons are added for you.
Console: Leads lists walkthrough and trial requests from the Contact page, with status, notes and Make their mountain. Each is also emailed to SITE_CONTACT_EMAIL.

Billing: choose your SummitOps plan, add-ons and monthly or yearly, and pay by card, US bank account or emailed invoice. Manage payment changes the card, shows receipts or cancels. New mountains start with a 14-day free trial.

If a payment fails or the trial ends, everything keeps working for 14 days with a notice at the top. After that SummitOps is read only until paid; patrol, the time clock and the Inbox always keep working.
Printing works again: the hand-off report, take-home instructions, refusal form and other patrol printouts were coming out blank.
Console: Plans and prices (with Sync to Stripe), a Billing column on the mountain list, and Change billing on each mountain for trials, free mountains and payments taken by check.

releases.title: Patrol operations, and fixes from an EMS review

notes.text: On duty: patrollers sign in when they reach the patrol room and out when they leave, on their phone or a shared patrol-room tablet. Dispatch now lists volunteers as well as paid patrollers, with their radio and station.
Phone alerts: turn them on for each phone, and you are alerted when dispatch sends you to a call, with On my way to answer. Critical calls alert everyone on duty, and can text responders too.

Closing sweep: set up routes of lifts and runs, give each to someone on duty, mark each stop as it is swept, call in anyone found, and call the mountain clear with the time. A late sweep raises an alert.

Opening checks: check each run (hazards marked, ropes and signs, padding) before opening it, or hold or close it with a reason. Mountain status updates at once, and runs now have a Hold status and a closure reason.

Medications: a formulary set by the medical director (authority, routes, largest dose, who may give it), stock by lot and expiry taken from as doses are given, controlled counts, and oxygen pressure and AED pad, battery and download tracking.

Giving a medication now checks the patient's allergies, and for nitroglycerin a recent blood pressure of at least 100 and no erectile dysfunction medication. Each patroller has a medical certification on the roster.
Tourniquet and pelvic binder treatments. A tourniquet's time shows at the top of the patient and of the hand-off sheet.

The hand-off sheet puts time-critical items first (tourniquet, stroke with last known well, cardiac arrest), then follows the MIST order, and now includes the primary survey, spinal motion restriction, and drugs or alcohol.

Reports check more before they are submitted: a head injury with loss of consciousness, amnesia or a low GCS does not go back to skiing without a written refusal or a named clearance; a refusal with drugs, alcohol or head injury signs needs a note on capacity; serious and transported patients need vitals.
Times in the future (23:45 typed for 13:45) are refused, and the vitals reminder stops once a patient has an outcome or is handed off.
Lost-person search on a case: who is missing and where last seen, search areas assigned to patrollers (who are alerted) and marked searched, and when and where they were found.
Checklists for a patroller or employee injured or exposed on duty, and for lift-related incidents (including notifying the state tramway inspector).
Daily log: one page per day built from everything recorded, with the leaders' notes, a sign-off, addenda after it, and search.
Lift evacuation: each lift's plan, equipment and patrollers needed, who on duty is ready, and drills that add a training record for each patroller.
Volunteer days: set the season's minimum, and each patroller sees their progress; reminders go to anyone short. Patrollers can be allowed to take open shifts themselves on Team, Cover.
Avalanche work, for mountains that turn it on: snow and hazard observations, and control shots by slide path with results, which can hold or close the run.
Records requests: log who asked for a report and on what authority, and release the approved report with a release number and a printable release pack. Cases can be put on legal hold.
Patrol settings: the medical director and protocol version, stamped on each report at sign-off, and the settings for the features above.
No signal: the last cases you opened can still be opened on your phone for 12 hours, and a new case started with no signal is sent when the signal returns.
Days patrolled now count the days people signed in on duty, and show each volunteer's days against the minimum.

releases.title: Patrol access from the staff page

notes.text: Edit details on a patroller’s staff page now has their patrol rank and patrol access level, so owners and managers can change them without going into Patrol.
Edit on the patrol roster always shows the access level. Patrol Admins, owners and managers can change it; everyone else sees who can.
The Needs staff housing option is gone from adding and editing staff.

Can’t make a patrol shift? Ask for cover on Patrol, Team, Cover. Everyone on the roster sees it there and in the Patrol shift cover conversation in the Inbox, and anyone free at that time can take it. The shift moves to them and you both get a message.
Those who build the patrol schedule can choose to approve each swap first. Taking a shift then sends an offer, and the shift moves once it is approved.
Shifts waiting for cover are marked Needs cover on the patrol schedule. Putting someone else on one from the schedule counts as covered.

releases.title: Patrollers from the staff page, and patrol permissions

notes.text: Add everyone on the staff page, as an employee or a volunteer. Tick On ski patrol, or press Put on ski patrol on their staff page, and they appear in Patrol.
Create login right from a person’s staff page, with a username filled in from their name and a temporary password.
Anyone on the patrol roster with a login can open Patrol, whatever their login role, so staff who also patrol no longer need a separate patrol login.
Patrol Admins can give one patroller extra permissions, or take one away, without changing everyone at the same access level (Team, Permissions).
The staff list shows who is a volunteer and who is on ski patrol, with a filter for each. Volunteers stay off the time clock and payroll.
Sign in with your username or your email. Everyone now has a username (you can change yours on Account), and your email still works if you have one.
Logins no longer need an email, except for owners and managers, so volunteers and seasonal staff can have their own sign-in.
Forgot your password? A manager sets a temporary one and tells you; you choose your own the next time you sign in.
Owner and manager password resets from the console can be temporary too. Existing logins were given usernames by the migration (first initial and last name, or the email before the @).

releases.title: Patrol keeps its own roster and schedule

notes.text: Patrol has its own schedule (Team, Schedule): a weekly grid of the roster, built and published by the patrol director and leads. Volunteers and paid patrollers are both scheduled here, and publishing messages each patroller their shifts.
Add patrollers straight to the roster, volunteers included, without a staff record. Paid patrollers can be on the staff list too, for pay and the time clock.
Days patrolled: each person’s days and hours this season, with a download for volunteer credit.
Today’s posts now lists who is on the patrol schedule for the day.

Staff and schedule shows patrol coverage in a read-only Patrol row; patrol shifts are made in Patrol. A paid patroller’s patrol time counts toward their hours, and they cannot be booked on a work shift and patrol at the same time.
My shifts shows your published patrol shifts alongside your work shifts.
The migration moves upcoming patrol shifts from Staff and schedule into the new patrol schedule and cancels the originals with a note; past ones stay as history.
The schedule is now a weekly grid: people down the side, days across, unfilled shifts in their own row, and each person’s hours for the week. On a phone it shows one day at a time.

Click any shift to change its time, position, person or note. When choosing who works it, the people who can work it come first with their hours that week, and anyone who cannot is listed with the reason.
Copy last week, or save a typical week as a template and apply it to any week. People are kept only where they can still work the shift.
When your manager publishes the schedule, you get a message in your Inbox listing your shifts, and another if one of your published shifts changes or is cancelled.
Hours: fix a missed clock-out or a wrong punch (with a reason, kept in the audit log), add a forgotten punch, approve the week, and export hours for payroll with overtime over 40 hours.
Each staff member has their own page: what they work as, certifications, availability, their login, their patrol and ski school roles, hours this week and upcoming shifts.
Staffing needs counts pass holders as well as tickets sold, and counts only filled shifts as covered.
Dates an instructor marks open on Instructor availability now count as available when scheduling, and someone who stops working comes off their future shifts automatically.
Opening someone’s availability, or a position’s required certifications, and saving no longer wipes what was saved. Both now open with what is saved.
Your availability in My shifts opens with what you saved before, and clocking in links your punch to the shift you are working.
SummitOps now has a version number, shown in Help and in your account menu, so you can tell at a glance which version you are using.
Help has a What's new page listing each update. Only the changes for your role and your mountain's apps are shown, and a small badge on Help tells you when there is something new.
The console shows the version that is live and every version that has been deployed, with when it first started and who deployed it.

deploy.sh says which version it is replacing, refuses to put an older version over a newer one (bash deploy.sh --allow-older to do it anyway), and checks that the new version is the one answering afterwards.

Inbox: send messages to one person or a group at your mountain, with links that open a customer, an order, a work order, a waiver, a document, an asset or a patrol case. Each person sees only the links their role can open.
A Share button on records sends a link to that record to someone in the Inbox.

Case review: when a patroller signs off a case, it goes to the review group (the Patrol Director and named backups), who approve it, send it back with comments or escalate it. The group chooses which kinds of case it reviews and gets a reminder after 72 hours.

releases.title: RFID cards and the injury network

notes.text: Gate: RFID cards. Load a pass onto a card, move it to a new card, and block a lost one. Cards are read by desk readers, by phone (NFC) or by camera.
Paired gates, turnstiles and handhelds check passes online and keep working from an offline list when the connection drops.
Two gates can no longer both let the same single-use ticket through, and a blocked card is always refused.
Injury network: mountains can choose to share de-identified injury counts and compare their numbers with similar mountains.
Guided tours walk new demo mountains through selling, the gate, patrol and more. The console has the network injury report.

releases.title: Waivers, the new case page, and assets

notes.text: Waivers: guests sign on a phone or tablet, with guardians for minors. You can look up who has signed, and every signed copy keeps the exact wording it was signed against.
A new patrol case page, with Care, Report and Record views, assessment tools, vitals, oxygen, medications, refusal and hand-off signatures. It saves on the phone when there is no signal.
Assets and fleet: one register for vehicles, lifts, snowmaking and buildings, with meters, fuel, inspections, service plans, parts, purchase orders, costs and QR labels.
Many small fixes and safety improvements from a full review of the app.
The database moved to Cloud SQL. Console operators sign in with their own email, password and authenticator, and the Demos page shows usage and lets you delete demos.
